meta.title: capy-flash v0.16.6: speed by engine part on one workstation
meta.about: This site is a guided view of a data collection: the measurements and supporting evidence produced for capy-flash v0.16.6, gathered in the technical report (PDF below) so that they can be shared and checked. The report is best read through an AI agent or searched for the number needed; this site walks through the same data by engine part and lets the reader explore it. Every number shown is taken from the report, with the table, figure or section it comes from; the column counts per round follow from the report's formula, clients × (drafts + 1). It was written by Claude (Anthropic) from the project's measurement records, under the direction of the project author.
meta.scope: The capy-flash LLM inference engine, v0.16.6, on one workstation: AMD Ryzen 9 9900X, 96 GB DDR5-5600, two RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB on PCIe 5.0 x8 + x8 without peer-to-peer (P2P) access. Models: Qwen3.8-27B (NVFP4, 3-bit), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (experts in system RAM; NVFP4, 64 GB), Inkling 2 Mini, SenseNova-Loop-9B (*, unreleased port). 27 November 2026, perf-max clocks (GPU unlocked, CPU boost on); fractions refer to ceilings measured on this machine.
meta.marks: C: computed in the report from measured inputs. *: SenseNova-Loop-9B, unreleased port; its numbers cannot be reproduced by others.

spec.conditions: One request, the 8 prose prompts of Appendix B1 (4 Italian, 4 English), 256 output tokens each, temperature 0, reasoning off; decode = Σ (tokens − 1) ÷ Σ decode time from the server's per-request timings, median of 2 passes; acceptance = accepted ÷ proposed drafts; tokens / round from the round log, or 1 + K × acceptance where no round log exists (C). v0.16.6 (9B: the port's binary), perf-max clocks, launcher flags. Flash-Next: steady state, acceptance range over two starts.
spec.function: A drafter proposes K tokens; the model verifies K + 1 columns in one pass. MTP: the model's multi-token head (--spec mtp, K = 1-5). DFlash2: a block drafter (27B NVFP4 default, K = 7). Prompt lookup: drafts copied from the prompt. --spec auto (Inkling 2 Mini): DSpark, DFlash2 or no drafter, chosen at every round.

v: A DFlash2 7 round yields 2.40 tokens on these prompts. DFlash2 7 and MTP 3 end 1.9 % apart (MTP 3 runs the 17.4 GB model file without DFlash2, as its launcher does).
DFlash2 is faster on the four English prompts (210-266 against 174-220 tok/s per prompt) and slower or level on the four Italian ones (119-152 against 139-162).
On code edits, JSON and quoting it is 33-98 % ahead of MTP 3 (Table 12). DFlash2 does not start without CUDA graphs (§12).
Prompt lookup on top of MTP 3 (the one-GPU default) proposes nothing on these prose prompts (other content: Table 12).
Each verified column routes its own experts. With MTP 3 the misses per generated token grow by 18 % (NVFP4, two GPUs) and 43 % (one GPU).
The share of the MTP 3 round that grows with the misses orders the gains: 60 % (NVFP4, one GPU, +16.5 %), 42 % (NVFP4, two GPUs, +40.3 %).
Two GPUs: passes without a drafter span 105.6-116.1 tok/s, a gain of +37 % to +50 % by pass.
With MTP 3 the misses per generated token grow by 21 % (64 GB, two GPUs) and 43 % (one GPU).
The share of the MTP 3 round that grows with the misses orders the gains: 46 % (64 GB, one GPU, +32.0 %), 22 % (64 GB, two GPUs, +45.0 %).
On the prose prompts the 64 GB edition decodes 24 % faster than NVFP4 with MTP 3 and 20 % faster without a drafter (§5).

conc.conditions: Closed loop, v0.16.6 (9B: the port's binary), perf-max clocks: N = 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 clients, client i starts at prompt i and sends its next prompt as soon as the previous answer ends; 256-token answers, temperature 0, reasoning off. After 10 s of load, one 40 s window per cell; throughput = tokens streamed to all clients in the window ÷ 40 s; per-request rate = total tokens ÷ total time from first to last streamed token. Launcher flags plus --max-concurrency 8; the draft setting is the one variable, on the same model file. Prose: the 8 prose prompts (33-38 tokens each); code: 8 code prompts (515-1,992 characters).
conc.function: --max-concurrency (1-8) batches the decode of several requests in one round; prompts are prefilled one at a time. With N requests and K drafts a verification round has N × (K + 1) columns. The 3-bit linear layers (source code: a small-batch kernel up to 8 tokens, a general GEMM from 9 to 63) and the Flash-Next expert kernels (README) have a fast path for up to 8 columns per round.

tie.text: Tie (≈): closed-loop throughputs within 10 % on Flash-Next (one 40 s window on one server start; start-to-start spread 10-13 %, Table C1) or within 1 % on the dense models (a repeated 27B no-drafter run reproduced its throughput within 0.1 %; the drafter arms were not repeated).

general.v: From 1 to 8 clients the throughput lead of each wider window over the next narrower one shrinks on every model and on both prompt sets. Whether it turns negative within 8 clients depends on acceptance.

v: MTP 3 leads MTP 1 at every N, and no drafter is last at every N.
DFlash2 7, a separate drafter with 8 columns per request, is 4 % ahead of MTP 3 at 1 client, a tie at 2, 10 % behind at 4 and 25 % behind at 8 clients, where it is level with no drafter (+1.6 %).
Acceptance does not change with N. Round time against columns was not measured on this model.
Of the 8 code prompts, seven ask the model to reprint the given code with a local change and one asks for new unit tests; a workload of new code was not measured.
Acceptance is constant with N: DFlash2 0.83-0.84 (6.8-6.9 tokens per round), MTP 3 0.95-0.96, MTP 1 0.99, the most favourable content for drafters measured in the report.
DFlash2 7 has the highest throughput at every N up to 8; its lead over MTP 3 shrinks from 85 % at 1 client to 73 %, 43 % and 22 % at 2, 4 and 8 clients (C).
Without a drafter the two prompt sets run at the same throughput within 2 % at every N.
MTP 3 is best up to 2 clients, MTP 1 at 4, no drafter at 8 (still rising at 8).

Each drafter loses throughput when a round grows from 8 to 16 columns: MTP 3 −51 % from 2 to 4 clients, MTP 1 −46 % from 4 to 8. The drop coincides with the 8-token threshold of the small-batch kernel read in the source; it was not profiled.
MTP 3 at 32 columns (8 clients) is above its value at 16 columns; these measurements do not explain it.
With the default MTP 3, four concurrent requests make 16 columns. One GPU with --max-concurrency 8 does not start (§12).
At 8 clients no drafter is the fastest window on both editions, 28-31 % ahead of MTP 1 and 64 % (NVFP4) / 55 % (64 GB) ahead of MTP 3. Below 8 clients the two best windows are within 4-7 %: ties.
MTP 3 at 4 and 8 clients: 133.2 and 118.1 tok/s against 142.2 with one client.

The concurrency configuration has fewer expert slots per layer at startup (--max-concurrency 8, base + elastic: MTP 3 56 + 23, MTP 1 57 + 23, none 61 + 21; one request: 64 + 23 and 68 + 21; Table 6); round logs were not taken with several clients.
At 8 clients no drafter is the fastest window on both editions, 28-31 % ahead of MTP 1 and 64 % (NVFP4) / 55 % (64 GB) ahead of MTP 3. Below 8 clients the two best windows are within 4-7 %: ties.
With MTP 3 the 64 GB edition stays above its one-client throughput (§12).

The concurrency configuration has fewer expert slots per layer at startup (--max-concurrency 8, base + elastic: MTP 3 77 + 30, MTP 1 77 + 30, none 83 + 29; one request: 87 + 30 and 92 + 29; Table 6); round logs were not taken with several clients.

With --draft-tokens 2 the port proposes 1.99 drafts per round at 1 and 2 clients and 1.00-1.01 at 4 and 8 (server log): one draft per round from 3 active requests on (rule read in the port's source); acceptance goes from 0.38 to 0.57.
It is ahead of no drafter at every N: +44 % at 1 client, +17 % at 8.

ctx.conditions: Context sweep, v0.16.6, perf-max clocks, launcher flags with the default drafter (9B: port configuration). The engine's own C++/CUDA sources cut at about 0.5k / 2k / 8k / 32k / 64k / 128k tokens, a unique prefix per request so that nothing is reused from cache (cold), "summarize file by file", 256 tokens, temperature 0; median of 3 rounds, lengths in alternating order. Prefill rate = prompt tokens ÷ the server's prompt time; prompt time = the server's time from request to first token. Up to each launcher's maximum context (3-bit 27B on one GPU: 65,536; 9B: 28,672 per request).

intro.v: At each prompt length of the context sweep: the prefill rate, the time to the first token and the decode of 256 tokens that follows. Decode with the default drafter at the longest prompt is 9-36 % below the shortest, over ranges that differ by model (26k to 131k tokens); no sweep without a drafter was taken.

ctx.function: Prompts run in chunks (27B: 2,048 tokens; Flash-Next: as wide as the expert cache can lend, up to 32,768). Flash-Next prefill chunks of at least 256 tokens (600 for the 64 GB edition on two GPUs) stream all non-resident experts over PCIe and run every expert on the GPU, copying the next layer under the current one. Prefill was not profiled in this campaign.

v: The 27B NVFP4 prefills fastest up to 32k tokens and slows at long contexts; Flash-Next starts slow and keeps its rate up to 131k.
Decode with the default drafter at the longest prompt is 9-36 % below the shortest, over ranges that differ by model (26k to 131k tokens), sd between rounds up to 29 tok/s; the 9B is not monotonic.

v: 27B NVFP4, default DFlash2 7, concurrent clients: on prose 586.5 tok/s at 8 clients against 778.9 with MTP 3 (−25 %); on code rewriting ahead of MTP 3 at 8 clients (+22 %). --spec mtp --draft-tokens 3 selects MTP 3 on the same model file.
27B 3-bit, more than 8 columns per round (two GPUs): −51 % throughput with MTP 3 from 2 to 4 clients, −46 % with MTP 1 from 4 to 8; with the default MTP 3, four concurrent requests make 16 columns.
27B 3-bit, one GPU, --max-concurrency 8: the server does not start (automatic KV sizing needs 5.68 GB, 5.16 GB free); the profile serves one request at a time.
Flash-Next NVFP4, MTP 3, 4 and 8 clients: 133.2 and 118.1 tok/s against 142.2 with one client; the 64 GB edition stays above one client.

Flash-Next NVFP4, four concurrent requests of 30-32k tokens (--max-concurrency 4): std::bad_alloc at admission in 3 of 3 attempts, with 11.1 GiB of RAM available; the pool is not identified. The flash-next-multi profile (KV in RAM) ran three such requests without error.

Flash-Next, one client in the closed loop: NVFP4 −5.7 % (no drafter) and −10.5 % (MTP 3), 64 GB edition −3.8 % and −3.5 %, against the one-request protocol; 4-5 points from the protocol, the rest a lower per-request decode rate.
DFlash2 with --no-cuda-graph: the server does not start; with graphs, the default, it runs; without a drafter eager mode works.

Flash-Next 64 GB, two GPUs, MTP 3, first start of the block: 174.6 and 189.9 tok/s with 13.44 ms rounds; the second start 197.5 and 200.8, a later start 198.7 and 202.2 with 12.02 ms rounds; cause not verified.
Flash-Next and the host: decode depends on the CPU and RAM that compute the missed experts; other CPUs and RAM were not measured.
Inkling 2 Mini: two GPUs, one request at a time; the engine supports neither one GPU nor concurrent requests for it.
SenseNova-Loop-9B*: unreleased port; drafter not measured on the one-request protocol.

Not measured: kernel profiles of the 3-bit 27B, of Flash-Next other than NVFP4 on two GPUs, and of prefill; round logs with several clients; round time against columns (27B NVFP4); concurrency on prompts that write new code; closed-loop concurrency of the 3-bit 27B on one GPU; PCIe fills without a drafter; a context sweep of Flash-Next NVFP4 on one GPU.
Engine

capy-flash v0.16.6 release binary (tag v0.16.6, commit fca2a736), launchers of the release tarball with default flags, no other workload on the machine. "2 GPUs" = tensor parallel 2. Explicit flags instead: the 9B port, the profiling runs, the 3-bit 27B's MTP 3 arm without prompt lookup.
Clocks
perf-max: GPU clocks unlocked and CPU boost on for the duration of a run. Every speed is at perf-max unless the row says eco.
One request

8 long prose prompts, 4 Italian and 4 English, sent one after the other; 256 output tokens each, temperature 0, reasoning off; 2 passes after one warm-up request, per server start. Decode = Σ (tokens − 1) ÷ Σ decode time from the server's per-request timings.
Flash-Next passes

Which experts sit in VRAM depends on what ran before: arms in the order A B B A (drafter, none, none, drafter), one server start each, 2 passes per start; first pass and steady state (median of passes 2-4) both given when they differ by more than 2 %.
Concurrent clients

N = 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 clients in a closed loop; after 10 s of load, a 40 s window. Checks: requests in decode in the window 0.93-0.99 × N on average; the server's own decode rate within −2.7 % to +4.2 % of the throughput.
Context sweep
The engine's own C++/CUDA sources (176 files, 1.84 MB) cut at the target length, a unique prefix per request so that nothing is reused from cache; median of 3 rounds.
Profiles

One 128-token request after warm-up under nsys. Eager runs (--no-cuda-graph): exclusive time per kernel on each GPU's streams. Graph runs: time per whole graph, no per-kernel split. A profiler that traces every launch adds its own cost per launch.
Bytes per token

Exact bytes of every weight object a decode step reads, from the model files' indices (for mixtures of experts: active experts × bytes per expert). Floor = bytes ÷ measured ceiling; share = floor ÷ whole measured step.
Marks
C: computed from measured inputs. *: SenseNova-Loop-9B, unreleased port; its numbers cannot be reproduced by others. Gains are computed from unrounded rates.
